plain_text:
MEETING MINUTES
Note: All proposals, presentations, and/or documentation to be reviewed and 
discussed at this meeting can be viewed online at the following link: 
https://bit.ly/SalemPACProposals
Meeting called to order at 6:31pm.
Roll Call PAC: Jim Bostick (Chair), Joseph “Joe” Badowski, Gwendolyn Rosemond, Brittany 
Minton, Bryan Apito. Becky Fisher joined after roll call.
Absent at Roll Call: Hannah Gathman; Becky Fisher (joined during the budget discussion).
Also Present: Staff: Julie Barry (Senior Planner Arts & Culture).
• Meeting Minutes Approval - October 20, 2026 Meeting Minutes
The Commission reviewed the October 20, 2026 meeting minutes. No corrections were raised. The 
motion to approve the minutes passed unanimously among members present. Mr. Bostick called for a 
vote to approve the minutes. Mr. Apito voted to approve. Mr. Badowski seconded. All members present 
voted to approve. 
• FY2027 Budget Update
Ms. Barry reported $11,643 in unallocated FY2027 funds. Members discussed potential allocations for 
public art mini grants, new or refurbished ArtBoxes, the decommissioned fire call boxes, and a potential 
new project that could require an initial $3,000–$5,000 contribution. The Commission agreed to revisit 
funding decisions in December, when more information is expected. No allocation was made.
Ms. Barry recommended that any calls for artists be issued in December or January, with selections 
made by February and projects completed by June 30, 2027. Mini grants have historically ranged from 
$500 to $2,500 per project. Mr. Apito suggested identifying potential indoor and outdoor locations for 
public art in the call. Members also discussed strategic placement of ArtBoxes beyond downtown and 
the conservation report’s recommendation to deaccession or repaint two existing boxes. Members were
encouraged to bring suggested locations to the December meeting.
• South Harbor Garage Window Art
Ms. Barry reported that revised designs from artist Erin Survilas were not yet available and will be 
brought back to the Commission once received. Mr. Bostick reported that he had worked with the artist 
to refine the concept and had seen improvements. No vote was taken.

• Other Projects and City Updates
Ferry Terminal Public Art: Ms. Barry reported that $100,000 in Footprint funds is designated for public 
art in the ferry terminal/waterfront area. The call for artists is on hold pending reconfiguration of the 
terminal interior. She anticipates bringing a draft call to the Commission for review in January or 
February.
Decommissioned Fire Call Boxes: The City is awaiting a decision from the Mayor on whether the boxes 
will be removed or made available for painting. Staff are also exploring whether removed boxes could 
be deaccessioned and auctioned. The Commission will revisit the project in December.
Sculpture Garden Loan Program: Ms. Barry reported that two of the six previously selected works were 
unavailable and that two ranked alternatives were available. The six proposed artists are Thomas 
Berger, Josie Campbell Dellenbaugh, Morris Norvin, Gary Rathmell, Janice Corkin Rudolf, and Allen 
Spivack.
Motion to approve the revised list of six artists is made by Mr. Apito, seconded by Mr. Bostick, and 
passes unanimously. Ms. Barry will proceed with contracts for the selected artists.
Ms. Fisher asked for feedback on the online ranking tool used in the selection process. Members found 
it helpful for gathering individual preferences. Ms. Barry emphasized that formal voting and deliberation
must take place at public meetings, and members noted the importance of keeping future use accessible
and transparent.
• Other Business
Social Media: Mr. Apito suggested revitalizing the City’s public art Instagram account to promote 
projects and opportunities. Ms. Fisher offered to help keep the account updated, and Mr. Bostick 
offered to provide training on Meta Business Suite. The Commission will continue the discussion.
Rousseau Collection Gift of Art: Ms. Barry reported that the agreement was awaiting the Superintendent
of Schools’ signature. Mr. Bostick reported that the works were framed and that he would finish 
photographing them. Once the agreement is executed, Ms. Barry will coordinate installation with school
facilities staff using the agreed-upon installation guidance. Members discussed the possibility of 
completing installation in time for the December 5 Salem 400 closing event at the high school, if 
feasible, or announcing the installation in January. Mr. Bostick will coordinate with Ms. Barry and Ms. 
Minton on timing.
• Adjournment
Mr. Bostick asks for a motion to adjourn. Motion to adjourn is made by Ms. Fisher, seconded by Mr. 
Apito, and all members present vote in favor.
Adjourn - The meeting adjourned at 7:16pm.
